note: The livecheck table (python -m wtdd.livecheck --list). One entry per hardware step. Keys: item (the roadmap item), step (<item>.<k>, k = the number or letter of the line under **Needs the dog** in that item's PR, the k of the evening's `live <item> <k>`), pr (the PR number the title is read from; null for a night-2 goal section), title (that Needs-the-dog line, verbatim), do (the physical action in one line, with what the eyes must confirm that no row can), rows (the ledger rows that must land, in order: {tool, agent?, ok, where: {dotted.path: value | {gte, lte, in, re}}}; empty = unchecked, cannot PASS), fatal_warns (regexes over the API log; a match is FAIL with the line), unsafe (only rows landing after the check starts count; {tool: T, before: U}: the order T then U is forbidden, the U row that completes it decides and is printed `U after T`; {tool: T, between: [A, B]}: a T row after an A row and before any B row is UNSAFE, the T row decides), timeout_s (FAIL when this many seconds have passed since the check started and a row is still missing; --timeout overrides it), settle_s (after the last row matched, keep watching the log and the unsafe patterns this long before PASS; 0 = PASS at once), note (what is a guess until the first live run). Thresholds marked UNVERIFIED were never read from a dog.
